subject: Request: Novus Therapeutics POC extension + one-time credits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novus — ask for POC extension + one-time credits (details & attachments)

Team,

Quick summary: Novus Therapeutics (Alice Chen) is in the middle of an IRB-driven delay for their data ingestion pipeline. They asked to extend the sandbox POC by 60 days because they can’t produce full test data until mid-May. The account is high strategic — they’re in discussions for a >$200k first-year ARR if the pilot succeeds.

Current ask: one-time 60-day POC extension + an additional $25k in complimentary platform credits (beyond our standard PLG allowance). They need runway to complete integration and run head-to-head evals on latency/cost with their internal inference.

Why I recommend approving:
- Strong product fit: our latency profile and quantization guidance are the primary reasons they picked Redwood.
- Near-term conversion signal: procurement has indicated a signed SOW is likely within 90 days after a successful POC.
- Competitive pressure: competitor X is offering longer sandbox windows; losing momentum risks them switching.

Commercial guardrails I propose if approved:
1) 60-day extension, capped at $25k credits.
2) Execution of a short MOU (mutual action plan attached) capturing success criteria and target signature within 90 days.
3) One-time trial clause: any further extensions require CRO/CEO signoff.

Attachments: Novus_POC_usage_report.pdf (current usage/time), Novus_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/NB-2026-0421
DocuSign (for MOU) placeholder: https://app.redwood.com/docs/DocuSignLink789

Request: can we get one-of approval (even conditional) to move quickly? If we prefer partial approval I can offer a 45-day extension + $15k credits to reduce risk.

Thanks,
Marissa
--
Marissa Cole | Senior AE, West
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0134

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novus — ask for POC extension + one-time credits (details & attachments)

Thanks for the summary, Marissa. Quick clarifying questions before I weigh in:
- Do we have a PO or any procurement signal, or is this purely PLG for now?
- What are the exact conversion milestones in the attached MAP (signing trigger / spend thresholds)?
- Any reason we can’t use time-limited feature flags or sandbox throttling instead of credits?

If procurement is close and the $200k ARR is realistic, I’m inclined to greenlight a smaller concession (45 days / $15k) with an explicit handoff to solutions + QBR cadence. If procurement is still several months out, we should tighten the success criteria.

Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer | Director, Deal Desk
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novus — ask for POC extension + one-time credits (details & attachments)

On Mon, Mar 21, 2026 at 11:03 AM Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Thanks for the summary, Marissa...

Marissa / Karthik — I reviewed the usage report and the MAP. High level: the product signals are strong and the risk to pipeline is real given competitor activity. I agree conversion probability is material (estimate ~55% given current exec engagement).

Decision (one-time, conditional approval):
- Approve a 45-day POC extension + $15,000 one-time credits (beyond PLG).
- Conditions: Novus signs the MOU within 7 business days of extension start; the MOU must include two measurable success criteria (latency target and cost-per-inference comparison).
- Agreement: if Novus requests any further extension or additional credits, it needs CRO (Vivek) signoff — no exceptions.

Rationale: gives them enough runway to unblock IRB ingestion while limiting downside. $15k is a reasonable concession vs $25k ask.

Marissa — please send the conditional approval to Alice and get the MOU signed. Karthik — please make sure legal/finance sees the MAP and we add a short SOW appendix to lock timing.

Priyom Das
Head of Strategic Deals (acting)
priyom_das@redwood.com
--
Note: I’m sending this from my mailbox; escalate to CRO if Novus pushes beyond this plan.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@novustx.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novus POC timeline — extension & one-time credits (conditional approval)

Alice — thanks for the update earlier. We discussed internally and can provide a one-time, conditional concession to help you finish the integration testing.

What we can offer immediately:
- 45-day POC extension starting when you confirm the extension (we’ll flip the sandbox flag).
- $15,000 one-time platform credit to be applied during the extension window.

Conditions:
1) Sign the attached MOU (I’ve attached the mutual action plan and a one-page MOU — DocuSign link below) within 7 business days of confirming the extension.
2) MOU must include two success criteria (we suggested latency < 150ms 95th and total cost per inference < $0.065) and target signature of full SOW within 90 days of extension start.
3) Any further changes require CRO signoff.

DocuSign (MOU): https://app.redwood.com/docs/DocuSignLink789
MAP attached: Novus_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx
Usage snapshot: Novus_POC_usage_report.pdf
HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/NB-2026-0421

If those terms work, confirm and I’ll route the DocuSign for your legal team. We’ll enable the extension as soon as the signed MOU returns.

Appreciate the partnership — we’re excited to get Novus running at scale.

Best,
Marissa
Senior AE, West
